title: On the Expressiveness of State Space Models via Temporal Logics
claim: Model variants form a hierarchy of expressiveness, each mapped to a logical fragment and bounded above by a known complexity class.
layout: Single diagram, bottom-to-top lattice of 5 nodes, dashed versus solid arrows, gray box
description: A bottom-to-top inclusion diagram of state space model variants. A light gray box labelled TC^0 (Merrill et al. 2024) covers most of the figure. Four bold node titles sit inside it: diagonal time-invariant gates at the bottom, diagonal gates at middle left, time-invariant gates at middle right, and mixed layers near the top. Outside the box, at the top, is SSM with arbitrary gates, which is at least REG. Each node has two lines. One line is labelled fin. prec. and the other log. prec. Each line is attached to a theorem or corollary reference by a bracket and a small arrow. Each line gives a lower bound in temporal-logic notation, such as pLTL_f, UN-pLTL_f, FO[<], MOD and the counting operator. Arrows between nodes show inclusion. Dashed arrows mark strict inclusions and solid arrows mark plain inclusions. The eye goes first to the bold titles and then up the arrows.
caption: Expressiveness hierarchy of SSM architectures mapped to logical fragments and complexity classes. We establish lower bounds for Diagonal, Time-Invariant, and Mixed SSMs, distinguishing between fixed-precision and log-precision (enabling counting operators $\backhash$). Dashed arrows indicate provably strict inclusions (Theorem [ref]). The gray box delineates the $TC^0$ upper bound from prior work [ref].
abstract: We investigate the expressive power of state space models (SSM), which have recently emerged as a potential alternative to transformer architectures in large language models. Building on recent work, we analyse SSM expressiveness through fragments and extensions of linear temporal logic over finite traces. Our results show that the expressive capabilities of SSM vary substantially depending on the underlying gating mechanism. We further distinguish between SSM operating over fixed-width arithmetic (quantised models), whose expressive power remains within regular languages, and SSM with unbounded precision, which can capture counting properties and non-regular languages. In addition, we provide a systematic comparison between these different SSM variants and known results on transformers, thereby clarifying how the two architectures relate in terms of expressive power.
